newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call at 3.5-4.0 pct, gilts seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call at 3.5-4.0 pct, gilts seen steady.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in a 3.5-4.0 percent range in early Monday trade, slightly up from the weekend close of 3.0-3.5 percent and dealers said they expect the day's trade to be range-bound.
"Supply and demand for funds is well-balanced at the moment," said a dealer. "Call money should be in a broad 3.5-4.0 percent range today."
Dealers said market attention will be on a bond auction to be held later today when the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) offers 50 billion rupees of four-year bonds.

"Trade should be cautious today as market players are a little uncertain about the cut-off yield the RBI will announce at the auction," said a dealer. "Market players are wary after the last auction."
At an auction of six-year bonds held on July 16, the RBI awarded a cut-off of 11.83 percent, well below market expectations of 11.90-11.95.
This led to a sizzling rally as bonds were re-priced on the new yield curve.
